Hi Karthik / Ben,

We’re reviewing the DPA obligations for NordicBank with respect to incident notification and evidence transfer. Two immediate asks:

1) When Redwood refers to "notify without undue delay" and your internal notify SLAs, what is the expected customer-facing timeline for (a) initial alert, (b) follow-up with scope, and (c) evidence availability for forensic review for EU-hosted workloads?

2) Cross-border evidence: if Redwood needs to deliver logs or object-level artifacts that contain customer personal data and some of those artifacts are in the US processing region, what steps do you take to (a) minimize transfer of personal data, (b) provide a legally defensible export (SCCs/processor-to-processor flow), and (c) handle requests where our regulators require data to remain within the EEA for forensics?

We’ve attached a short list of DPA questions (NordicBank_DPA_Questions.pdf). Please respond with your recommended operational timelines and the typical gating items for evidence export. Also include a primary on-call contact for escalations.

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Laura (legal) and Ben (ops) are cc’d to add details and operational constraints.

Summary (operational baseline):
- Initial alert: within 24 hours of confirmation of a security incident affecting customer data. This is a short-form notification with known scope and next steps.
- Scope update: a follow-up within 72 hours where we provide an estimated scope and whether PII was plausibly affected.
- Evidence availability: we aim to make forensics artifacts available for secure transfer within 7-10 business days, subject to legal gating (court orders, regulator requests) and redaction needs.

Cross-border approach:
- Minimize transfers: we prioritise EEA-region artifact export by using region-specific snapshots and prefix-filtered logs where feasible.
- Legal mechanics: for exports that involve US-hosted artifacts, we rely on processor-to-processor flow with SCCs in place (we can provide a template).
- EEA-only requirement: where regulator requires evidence to remain within the EEA, we can perform on-site/excerpted forensics (export controlled) or transfer a sanitized package; acceptance of this approach needs to be listed in the DPA appendix.

Gating items that may extend timelines:
- Need for a formal evidence request (signed) and POA for regulator-facing disclosures.
- Export approvals if artifacts include third-party subprocessor data (legal review).
- If an incident triggers law enforcement involvement, export timelines may be delayed pending legal direction.

On-call escalation: ben_carter@redwood.ai (Ops Escalation), +1-650-555-0187 (US mobile) — available as our primary technical liaison.

Laura / Ben — can you confirm the 7-10 business day evidence window and the redaction workflow? Also, Laura, note Maria’s regulator EEA-retention preference.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Hi Maria — quick legal note and next steps from Redwood legal.

1) Evidence request form: to proceed we need a signed Evidence Request Form that outlines the scope, purpose, and retention limits for the exported artifacts. This reduces scope creep and gives our forensics team clear parameters. I’ve attached a draft form (Redwood_Evidence_Request_Form.docx).

2) Redaction & minimisation: for EEA-only requirements we typically provide a filtered export (prefix and time-range limited) and perform a PII redaction pass where practical. If regulators demand raw-level artifacts within the EEA, we will propose a controlled on-site extraction or a secure remote session that keeps the raw data in-region. Both options require a written agreement on data handling.

3) Subprocessor notices: if any of the artifacts involve a third-party subprocessor (e.g., logging or CDN providers), we will route those requests through our Subprocessor Liaison. That can add 2-4 business days for approvals. We’ll flag subprocessor involvement in the scope update.

4) SLA language proposal: we can add an appendix to the DPA with the following operational commitments:
   - initial notification: 24 hours from confirmation of incident (business hours defined in DPA);
   - scalable scope update: 72 hours;
   - evidence availability: 10 business days for full forensic package, subject to legal gating and subprocessor approvals;
   - expedited path: where customer provides a signed evidence request and covers approved expedited egress costs, we will use a 3-5 business day target.

Please confirm that NordicBank can sign the Evidence Request Form and whether you need an explicit EEA-only processing addendum. Once received we’ll route the request to forensics and subprocessor teams.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
